How does it work? ↗

1. Choose private keys

q and α are public. Alice chooses XA and Bob chooses XB. Their private keys stay with them.

2. Exchange public keys

Each calculates Y = αX mod q. Alice sends YA to Bob, and Bob sends YB to Alice.

3. Calculate the secret

Each calculates K = (received Y)private X mod q. Both arrive at the same result. The secret itself is never sent.

What if someone intercepts the exchange? Basic Diffie–Hellman doesn’t authenticate identities. An attacker can replace the public keys and share a secret with each person. Verified signatures and certificates prevent this substitution.
